observation.visible_scene: A flooded grove of slender, feathery-leaved trees (trunks emerging directly from murky green-brown water) under an overcast sky. A bright vertical reflection of the sky runs down the center of the water, flanked by dark tree reflections. Two semi-transparent watermark overlays are present: 'Full HD / WINYEDA' top-right and 'YouTube : WINYEDA' bottom-right. A thin line of floating debris/logs sits near the tree bases on the right mid-ground. No people, boats, or animals are visible.
visible_changes: The camera performs a slow pan to the right: the left tree trunk shifts from ~x130 (frame 1) to ~x65 (frame 41), and the right trunk from ~x950 to ~x870, so the whole grove drifts leftward in the frame while the trunks remain fixed in the water (camera motion, not object motion).

The water surface shows continuous small ripples; the bright central sky-reflection and the dark tree-reflections deform and break up differently from frame to frame, indicating ongoing local surface motion.
The floating debris line and the tree trunks keep a constant relative position to each other, confirming they are static scene elements rather than moving objects.
The foliage is essentially stable frame-to-frame, with at most very slight edge movement (no clear wind sway resolvable).
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the flooding and the water level change are not shown.
Whether the ripples are from raindrops, wind, or an unseen disturbance is not determinable from the frames.
What lies beyond the left/right/top/bottom frame edges, and whether the pan continues after the crop, is unknown.
uncertain_details: Exact pan direction/magnitude is inferred from consistent leftward drift of static trunks; background cues are weak but the trunks themselves support the interpretation.
Any minor leaf sway is not confidently distinguishable from compression artifacts.
The bright central band is a sky reflection, not a separate object or open gap in the water.
